title: Ledger reports filter the period in SQL and require ISO dates
detail: `report:balances`, `report:income-statement` and `report:balance-sheet` now pass `from`/`to` and the posted status to the database query, so a report reads only the entries it sums. Both bounds stay inclusive. `from` and `to` must be calendar dates in the form `YYYY-MM-DD`; other strings fail validation instead of being compared as text.
migration: Callers that pass `from` or `to` send `YYYY-MM-DD` dates.

title: create-transaction books at most once per sourceRef
migration: Apps that mount ledger run `kumiko-schema generate` and ship the migration that adds `read_ledger_transactions.source_ref` and its unique index. Callers that guard repeat bookings by searching `reference` pass `sourceRef` instead.

title: Idempotent ensure-accounts write
migration: Replace app-side find-or-create loops over account:list and account:create with one ensure-accounts call.

title: Ledger reversal and schedule links moved out of reference
detail: Reversals set reversesTransactionId (unique per tenant), confirmed schedule periods set scheduleId and period, and the Storno copies scheduleId, period and subject from its original. create-transaction accepts an optional period but can no longer forge a reversal or a booked period through reference. Reversing a Storno is rejected with transaction_is_reversal. scheduleReference was removed; findReversedIds and LedgerTxRow use the new columns.
migration: Replace scheduleReference matching with LedgerTxRow.scheduleId/period and read reversals via reversesTransactionId. Load schedule bookings with ledger:query:schedule-actuals instead of paging the transaction list. Transaction events are now eventVersion 2; an upcaster derives reversesTransactionId from a v1 Storno's reference and scheduleId/period from `schedule:<id>:<period>` (a v1 Storno copies them from its original), so rebuilding read_ledger_transactions restores the links of existing bookings. When several v1 bookings name the same original (a double Storno click or a free reference with another booking's id), only the first in event order gets reversesTransactionId; the others keep their reference as display text, so the rebuild does not fail on the unique index.

title: Subject totals and schedule actuals queries
migration: Replace loops that page ledger:query:transaction:list per contract or schedule with one call to these queries.

title: New indexes on ledger transactions, job runs and job run logs
migration: Apps that mount ledger or jobs run `kumiko-schema generate` and ship the resulting migration.

title: ledger confirm-schedule-period takes its lock through TenantDb
The deprecated ledgerFeature constant is removed
detail: ledgerFeature was kept next to createLedgerFeature() for one release. Mount the feature by calling createLedgerFeature().
migration: Run bun kumiko-upgrade --apply. It replaces ledgerFeature with createLedgerFeature().

title: Document the duplicate check required before the (tenant_id, source_ref) unique index
migration: Before upgrading, check each database for duplicates and clean them up: SELECT tenant_id, source_ref, count(*) FROM read_ledger_schedules WHERE source_ref IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING count(*) > 1; Any row returned makes the unique index migration abort.

title: confirm-schedule-period serializes concurrent confirms of the same schedule period
Schedule sourceRef is unique per tenant (partial unique index read_ledger_schedules_tenant_id_source_ref_uidx)
migration: sourceRef is now unique per tenant: a second createSchedule (or updateSchedule) with a sourceRef already used in the same tenant fails with unique_violation (HTTP 409). Schedules without a sourceRef and the same sourceRef in different tenants stay allowed. Before applying, check for duplicates: SELECT tenant_id, source_ref, count(*) FROM read_ledger_schedules WHERE source_ref IS NOT NULL GROUP BY tenant_id, source_ref HAVING count(*) > 1; and resolve them through real writes (updateSchedule with another sourceRef). kumiko schema generate treats the new unique index on a managed projection as destructive (DROP TABLE + CREATE TABLE + .rebuild.json); a rebuild would also hit the unique index on historical duplicates. Hand-edit the generated migration: replace the generated DROP/CREATE with exactly DROP INDEX IF EXISTS "read_ledger_schedules_tenant_id_source_ref_idx"; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "read_ledger_schedules_tenant_id_source_ref_uidx" ON "read_ledger_schedules" ("tenant_id", "source_ref") WHERE "source_ref" IS NOT NULL; and discard the generated .rebuild.json (delete the file, do not commit it). Code that does find-then-create by sourceRef should expect unique_violation on create and re-read the schedule that won the race.

title: ledger create-transaction and reverse-transaction resolve agent risk high
A ledger schedule needs subjectType and subjectId together or neither
migration: Create and update schedule calls that set only one of the two fields now fail validation. Send both fields or neither.

title: Ledger schedules get an optional filterable sourceRef field
migration: Run `kumiko schema generate`. For a new nullable column and a new non-unique index on a managed projection it emits an in-place `ALTER TABLE "read_ledger_schedules" ADD COLUMN "source_ref" text` plus a `CREATE INDEX`, with no DROP/CREATE and no `.rebuild.json`. No backfill: do not write the column with SQL. Old schedules stay at `sourceRef = null`, so callers should fall back to their previous lookup key for them.

title: Account code is unique per tenant (partial unique index read_ledger_accounts_tenant_id_code_uidx)
detail: `accountEntity` declares `read_ledger_accounts_tenant_id_code_uidx`, a unique index on `(tenant_id, code)` that only covers accounts with a code. Two parallel find-then-create calls for the same code (two tabs, two devices) could each create an account and leave a tenant with duplicate codes. The second write now fails with `unique_violation` (HTTP 409). This applies to `createAccount` and to an `updateAccount` that changes the code. Accounts without a code are unaffected, and the same code in different tenants stays allowed.
migration:
Before you apply the migration, check for existing duplicates:

  SELECT tenant_id, code, count(*) FROM read_ledger_accounts
  WHERE code IS NOT NULL GROUP BY tenant_id, code HAVING count(*) > 1;

`kumiko schema generate` treats a new unique index on a managed projection as destructive. It emits DROP TABLE + CREATE TABLE plus a `.rebuild.json`, which means a full event replay of `read_ledger_accounts`. A rebuild creates the table's indexes before it replays. So if a tenant's event history ever contained two accounts with the same code at the same time, the replay hits the unique index and fails, even after one of them was renamed. For an app with existing ledger data, hand-edit the generated migration before committing it. Replace the DROP/CREATE with an in-place

  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "read_ledger_accounts_tenant_id_code_uidx"
    ON "read_ledger_accounts" ("tenant_id", "code") WHERE "code" IS NOT NULL;

and delete the `.rebuild.json`. The migrations snapshot stays as generated. If the duplicate check found rows, resolve them first through real writes, for example an `updateAccount` that gives the extra account another code. Never edit the table directly. For such a tenant, a later full rebuild of `read_ledger_accounts` still replays the historical duplicate and fails. An app that already created this index by hand under the same name (money-horse migration 0024) gets a no-op from the in-place statement.

Code that does find-then-create by code should expect `unique_violation` on create and re-read the account that won the race.
